description: In apply_body_value_args, when maxBodyValueBytes truncates a bodyValue, the code walks back from the byte limit to find the last valid UTF-8 char boundary: while !text.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }. A contributor might simplify this to &text[..limit] or use truncate(limit), but those would panic on multi-byte UTF-8 sequences if limit falls inside a codepoint. The comment correctly notes this is O(1) since multi-byte sequences are at most 4 bytes, so at most 3 iterations. This is the correct, standard Rust pattern for safe UTF-8 truncation.
title: maxBodyValueBytes truncation walks back to UTF-8 char boundary to avoid producing invalid JSON
